cells.tense: You're in the give-and-take of it right now, and your hand is steady on it — the scale evens without anyone keeping the tally, because both of you are holding the same thing true.
cells.ask: Offer one exchange more open than the last one you counted — and let the return arrive on its own timing.
cells.core:
Right now you're in an even exchange and you know it. You give what's actually yours to give, you take what's actually offered, and the fairness runs without a ledger. In the work of becoming yourself, this is what it looks like when it's going well — you don't dim what you've got to keep the peace, and you don't take more than your share to prove something. People feel the steadiness in how you deal with them, and it holds.

That steadiness isn't the end of anything. It can be handed forward — one more openness than you'd usually risk, and the return gets to land when it lands. What's even between you and someone else doesn't have to be guarded. It can be spent, and spending it is what feeds what comes next.
cells.sheetLine: You give and receive in fair measure, and it's steady.

cells.tense: You're already living in the version where the scales come even, bracing for the settling-up that hasn't happened — and you're treating it like it's here.
cells.ask: Take one thing you can carry on your own and leave the exchange with that person settled for now — let it hold without you pushing it toward fairness.
cells.core:
You're reaching ahead of the exchange to force it even. Every give gets watched for its return, every debt gets tracked to the decimal, and you're braced for the settlement before the other person has had a chance to respond. Fairness starts to look like something you impose on the moment instead of something the two of you find together — and when it's imposed, what's real in you can't show.

The strength to hold something steady without forcing it is available. Not to correct the exchange, but to let it stand. Carry what's actually yours, on your own, and stop reaching for the balancing moment. What you're already holding is enough; it doesn't need a verdict attached.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing the scales even before anything's actually owed.

cells.tense: You stopped giving and stopped taking a while back, and you're still standing where the exchange went quiet — the door's behind you, and your hand's off it.
cells.ask: Sit with one thing you know clearly — just what you can see — and let that be the practice, without needing to send it anywhere yet.
cells.core:
Giving and receiving moved through you easily once, and now the room is quiet. That ease is where you left it, and the exchange isn't happening. The capacity itself hasn't gone — what's missing is the reach. In a life where you're becoming what you are, going quiet on the exchange means part of you is still waiting at a door that's already closed behind you.

What brings a person back into exchange isn't pushing harder at the exchange. It's the smaller practice underneath it: noticing what's actually true in front of you, one thing at a time, until the noticing feels steady enough to trust. Do that in private for a while. The reaching comes back on its own once the ground feels solid under it.
cells.sheetLine: You've gone quiet on the exchange, and you're still back at the point where it stopped.

cells.tense: You're already fair in how you deal with people — generously, evenly, more than most — and calling it just being decent, as if it were the world's doing and not yours.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already know is the right way to treat someone — out loud, once, and own that knowing as yours.
cells.core:
You're already running an even exchange with the people around you — adjusting, giving what's needed, taking what's offered, keeping it fair without making a production of it. That's real, and it's shaping how people experience you. You just don't call it anything you're doing.

The knowing underneath it is quieter than the acting on it. Before you fix the next imbalance, notice that you already know what the right thing is — the perception arrives before you decide to apply it. Say one of those knowings out loud, plainly, as yours. The fairness doesn't need defending. It needs to be claimed.
